documents.title: Ministry Order on Typing Standards
documents.text: The Ministry of Public Administration has issued a comprehensive order regarding the maintenance of typing standards in all government offices across Bangladesh. Every computer operator and typist employed in any ministry, directorate, or attached department must ensure that all official documents including letters, memorandums, circulars, notices, and annual reports are typed with absolute accuracy. Spelling mistakes, punctuation errors, and incorrect spacing will not be tolerated under any circumstances. A special quality assurance committee has been formed at the secretariat level to conduct random inspections of typed documents. This committee will submit a monthly report to the joint secretary regarding the performance of each computer operator. Any operator found to have more than five typing errors in a single official letter will receive a written warning. Three written warnings within six months will lead to a formal disciplinary proceeding. This order is issued with the approval of the senior secretary and is effective from the first day of next month. All section officers are directed to inform their subordinate staff about these strict guidelines immediately.

documents.title: Notice for Competitive Typing Examination
documents.text: The Bangladesh Public Service Commission hereby publishes a notice for the upcoming competitive typing examination for the recruitment of computer operators in various government ministries. The examination will be held on the twenty fifth day of next month at designated centers in Dhaka, Chittagong, Rajshahi, Khulna, Barisal, Sylhet, Rangpur, and Mymensingh. Candidates must report to their assigned centers by eight thirty in the morning. The typing test will begin at nine o'clock sharp and will continue for exactly five minutes. No extra time will be given under any circumstances. Each candidate will be provided with a standard desktop computer and a QWERTY keyboard. The passage to be typed will appear on the screen. Candidates must type the passage exactly as shown without changing any word or punctuation. The evaluation will be based on both speed and accuracy. A minimum speed of thirty five words per minute with ninety percent accuracy is required to pass. Candidates are strictly prohibited from bringing mobile phones, smart watches, or any other electronic devices into the examination hall. Any violation of these rules will result in immediate disqualification and cancellation of the candidacy.

documents.title: Office Memorandum on Weekly Reporting
documents.text: The Establishment Division of the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh has issued an important memorandum regarding the submission of weekly typing reports by all computer operators. Every operator working in any section of the secretariat or any attached office must prepare and submit a detailed report every Friday before leaving the office. The report must be typed in the prescribed format which includes the total number of letters typed during the week, the number of errors corrected, the average typing speed achieved, and the names of officers for whom typing work was completed. The report must also mention any technical issues faced with the computer or keyboard during the week. The section officer will review each report and sign it before forwarding it to the deputy secretary. Any operator who fails to submit the report for two consecutive weeks will have their salary delayed for the following month. This memorandum is part of a larger initiative to increase transparency and accountability in office administration. All senior officials are requested to ensure that their subordinate staff comply with this new requirement strictly. The memorandum will remain in force until further notice from the ministry.

documents.title: Circular Regarding Promotion of Computer Operators
documents.text: The Ministry of Finance has published a detailed circular regarding the promotion policy for computer operators working in different government offices. According to this new circular, promotion from the position of junior computer operator to senior computer operator will no longer be based solely on seniority. Candidates must now pass a departmental typing examination conducted by the ministry's examination committee. The examination will consist of two parts. The first part is a five minute typing test where candidates must achieve a minimum speed of forty five words per minute with ninety five percent accuracy. The second part is a short written test on office procedures and basic computer knowledge. Only those who pass both parts will be considered for promotion. Additionally, candidates must have completed at least eight years of continuous service in the current grade. The circular also states that any operator who has received more than two written warnings for typing errors in the last three years will be disqualified from appearing in the promotion examination. Applications for the promotion examination must be typed in the standard format and submitted to the deputy secretary within thirty days of the publication of this circular. This new policy aims to ensure that only the most skilled and dedicated employees receive promotion to higher positions.

documents.title: Duty Assignment and Transfer Order
documents.text: The undersigned, acting under the authority granted by the Ministry of Public Administration, hereby issues a duty assignment and transfer order for the following computer operators with immediate effect. Mr. Abdur Rahim, currently posted in the finance section of the main secretariat, is hereby transferred to the budget section. He must report to the new section within three working days. Ms. Fatema Begum, currently working in the establishment division, is promoted and transferred to the training cell as senior computer operator. Mr. Kamal Hossain, who has been serving in the accounts section for the last five years, is transferred to the audit section. All concerned individuals must complete the handover process properly before leaving their current posts. A relieving letter must be typed in duplicate and signed by both the outgoing operator and the receiving section officer. One copy will remain in the personal file of the employee and the other copy will be kept in the section record. Any operator who fails to report to the new section within the specified time without prior written approval will be considered absent from duty and disciplinary action will be taken accordingly. This transfer order is part of a routine administrative reshuffle and does not affect the pay scale or other benefits of the employees. All section officers are requested to facilitate a smooth transition for the transferred staff.

documents.title: Standard Format for Official Letters
documents.text: The Directorate of Administration has issued a directive reminding all computer operators about the standard format for typing official letters in government offices. Every official letter must begin with the full name and address of the sending office typed at the top right corner. The date must be typed below the address in the format day, month, and year. The subject line must be typed in bold capital letters and underlined. The body of the letter should be divided into clear paragraphs. The first paragraph should state the purpose of the letter. The middle paragraphs should provide necessary details and explanations. The final paragraph should clearly state the expected action from the recipient. The sender's designation must be typed at the bottom left corner followed by the office seal. The name and signature of the sender should appear below the designation. If the letter has an attachment, the word enclosure must be typed at the bottom left corner below the signature line. All letters must be typed in Times New Roman font with size twelve. The line spacing must be set to one point five. Margins must be set to one inch on all sides. Any letter that does not follow this standard format will be returned to the computer operator for retyping. Repeated failure to follow the format will result in a written warning being placed in the employee's file. This directive is effective immediately and applies to all sections of the ministry.

documents.title: Application Procedure for Annual Leave
documents.text: All computer operators and office staff are hereby informed about the correct procedure for submitting applications for annual leave. Every leave application must be typed on a clean white sheet of paper using the standard government format. The subject line should clearly state the type of leave being requested such as annual leave, casual leave, or sick leave. The body of the application must mention the exact number of days requested and the specific dates from which the leave will start and end. A valid reason for taking the leave must be typed clearly. The application must be addressed to the deputy secretary of the respective section. The applicant must type their full name, designation, employee identification number, and the date of submission at the bottom of the application. The application must then be signed by the applicant in blue ink. No application will be accepted without a proper signature. The application should be submitted to the section officer at least seven working days before the intended start of the leave. In case of emergency sick leave, the application must be submitted within two days of returning to office along with a medical certificate from a registered physician. Any leave taken without prior approval will be marked as unauthorized absence and will result in deduction of salary. All computer operators are advised to keep a typed copy of every leave application for their personal record. This procedure has been approved by the senior secretary and any violation will be treated as misconduct.

documents.title: Notification on Data Entry Accuracy
documents.text: The Ministry of Planning has issued an urgent notification regarding the critical importance of data entry accuracy in all government offices. With the increasing digitization of public records including land documents, birth certificates, national identity cards, and pension files, the role of computer operators has become more important than ever before. A single typing mistake in a land record can cause years of legal dispute between citizens. Similarly, an incorrect digit in a pension file can deprive a retired government employee of their rightful benefits. Therefore, every computer operator must treat every data entry task with the highest level of concentration and care. The notification introduces a new verification system where every typed document must be checked by a second operator before final submission. The second operator will be responsible for identifying any spelling mistakes, numerical errors, or formatting issues. Both the original typist and the verifier must sign a declaration stating that the document is error free. If any error is discovered after submission, both operators will be held equally responsible and will face disciplinary action. The ministry has also announced that operators with consistently error free performance will receive a quarterly cash reward and a certificate of appreciation. This notification is part of the government's commitment to providing accurate and reliable digital services to the citizens of Bangladesh.

documents.title: Guidelines for Maintaining File Register
documents.text: The Department of Records and Archives has published detailed guidelines for computer operators regarding the proper maintenance of the official file register. Every section of every ministry and directorate must maintain a digital file register that is updated daily by the designated computer operator. The register must contain the following information for each file: the file number, the date of creation, the subject matter, the name of the originating officer, the current location of the file, the date of each movement, and the final disposal date. All entries must be typed clearly using the prescribed format. No overwriting or correction fluid is allowed on the printed register. If an error is made, the operator must type a new entry and clearly mark the old entry as cancelled. The register must be printed and signed by the section officer at the end of every working day. A backup copy of the digital register must be saved on the office server every Friday. Any file that cannot be located through the register will be treated as lost, and the computer operator responsible for updating the register will be held accountable. The guidelines also state that all computer operators must receive training on proper file management within three months of their appointment. The department will conduct surprise audits of the file register every quarter to ensure compliance. These guidelines are effective from the first day of the next financial year.

documents.title: Code of Conduct for Government Typists
documents.text: The Ministry of Establishment has published a revised code of conduct specifically for computer operators and typists working in all government offices across Bangladesh. Every operator must read this code carefully and sign a declaration stating that they will follow all rules. The code includes the following key provisions. First, no operator shall share any confidential typed document with any unauthorized person including family members or friends. Second, operators are strictly prohibited from using office computers for personal work such as typing resumes, personal letters, or social media posts during office hours. Third, every operator must keep their workstation clean and organized at all times. Fourth, operators must report any malfunction of their computer or keyboard immediately to the IT section. Fifth, operators must not install any unauthorized software on office computers. Sixth, operators must log out of their accounts and shut down their computers properly at the end of each working day. Seventh, operators must maintain a professional and respectful attitude toward all colleagues and officers. Any violation of this code will result in a formal inquiry by a disciplinary committee. Depending on the severity of the violation, the committee may issue a warning, impose a fine, suspend the operator, or recommend termination of employment. All operators are advised to keep a printed copy of this code on their desk for easy reference. This code supersedes all previous codes issued on this subject.

documents.title: Instructions for Handling Urgent Typing Tasks
documents.text: The Cabinet Division has issued special instructions for computer operators regarding the handling of urgent typing tasks that require immediate attention. In any government office, certain documents such as presidential orders, emergency notifications, court directives, and disaster management communications may require typing and dispatch within a very short timeframe. When such an urgent task arrives, the computer operator on duty must give it the highest priority and set aside all routine typing work. The operator must type the document with maximum concentration while maintaining accuracy. Speed is important in urgent tasks but not at the cost of correctness. After typing, the operator must read the entire document aloud in their mind to catch any hidden errors. If the document contains numerical data such as dates, amounts, or identification numbers, the operator must double check each digit against the original handwritten copy. The operator must then print two copies of the typed document. One copy will be sent to the authorized officer for signature and the other copy will be kept in the urgent file register. The operator must also make a digital backup of the document on a secure drive. If the operator makes a mistake in an urgent document that causes a delay in official business, a formal inquiry will be conducted. Repeated failure in handling urgent tasks will be considered incompetence and may lead to transfer to a less demanding section. These instructions have been approved by the cabinet secretary and are effective immediately.

documents.title: Notice Regarding Annual Confidential Report
documents.text: The Ministry of Public Administration has published a notice regarding the preparation of the annual confidential report for all computer operators and typists. The annual confidential report is a comprehensive evaluation of an employee's performance over the entire financial year. For computer operators, the report includes several specific criteria. The first criterion is typing speed measured in words per minute based on monthly tests. The second criterion is accuracy measured by the percentage of error free documents typed. The third criterion is punctuality including daily attendance and timely submission of reports. The fourth criterion is behavior and cooperation with colleagues and officers. The fifth criterion is the ability to handle urgent and emergency typing tasks. The sixth criterion is the maintenance of office equipment and proper shutdown procedures. The section officer will prepare the draft report based on daily observations and monthly records. The draft will then be reviewed by the deputy secretary. The final report will be signed by the joint secretary and placed in the employee's personal file. Any computer operator who receives a poor rating for three consecutive years will not be eligible for promotion. Operators who receive excellent ratings for five consecutive years will be recommended for accelerated promotion and a cash award. Every operator has the right to see their annual confidential report and submit a written appeal if they disagree with any part of the evaluation. The appeal must be typed in the standard format and submitted within fifteen days of receiving the report.

documents.title: Directive on Use of Shortcut Keys
documents.text: The Information Technology Division of the Government of Bangladesh has issued a directive encouraging all computer operators to learn and use keyboard shortcut keys to increase productivity. Using shortcut keys reduces the need to switch between the keyboard and the mouse, which saves valuable time during busy office hours. The directive lists the most important shortcut keys that every operator should memorize. For copying text, use control key together with the letter C. For cutting text, use control key together with the letter X. For pasting text, use control key together with the letter V. For saving a document, use control key together with the letter S. For undoing a mistake, use control key together with the letter Z. For selecting all text in a document, use control key together with the letter A. For making text bold, use control key together with the letter B. For italicizing text, use control key together with the letter I. For underlining text, use control key together with the letter U. For finding a specific word in a document, use control key together with the letter F. For printing a document, use control key together with the letter P. The directive states that all new computer operators will be tested on their knowledge of these shortcut keys during the probation period. Operators who consistently use shortcut keys will be able to complete typing tasks faster and with less physical strain. The directive also recommends that operators practice these shortcuts until they become automatic habits. This small investment in learning will yield significant returns in daily productivity and career advancement.

documents.title: Circular on Office Timing and Attendance
documents.text: The Ministry of Establishment has issued a revised circular regarding office timing and attendance procedures for all computer operators and office staff. According to this circular, all government offices will operate from nine in the morning to five in the evening from Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday will be weekly holidays. Every computer operator must mark their attendance by typing their name, employee identification number, and arrival time into the digital attendance register immediately upon entering the office. The register automatically records the exact time of entry. Any operator who arrives after nine fifteen will be marked as late. Three late arrivals in one month will result in a half day salary deduction. Any operator who arrives after ten in the morning without prior written approval will be marked as absent for the full day. Before leaving the office at the end of the day, every operator must again type their departure time into the attendance register. Operators are required to remain in the office until five in the evening unless they have received special permission for early departure. The attendance register is automatically backed up to the central server every hour. The deputy secretary will review the attendance records at the end of every month. Operators with perfect attendance for six consecutive months will receive a special attendance bonus. This circular is effective from the first day of next month and supersedes all previous circulars on office timing.

documents.title: Guidelines for Typing Budget Documents
documents.text: The Ministry of Finance has issued special guidelines for computer operators who are assigned the responsibility of typing budget related documents. Budget documents contain highly sensitive financial data including revenue estimates, expenditure allocations, and development project costs. A single typing error in a budget document can lead to incorrect financial planning and misallocation of government funds. Therefore, operators handling budget documents must follow these strict guidelines. First, all budget documents must be typed in a separate secure computer that is not connected to the internet. Second, after typing each page, the operator must compare the typed text with the original handwritten document line by line. Third, any numerical figure must be verified by at least two different operators independently. Fourth, the operator must save a backup copy of every budget document on an encrypted drive. Fifth, no budget document shall be printed until it has been approved by the finance officer. Sixth, printed copies of budget documents must be kept in a locked cabinet. Seventh, operators are strictly prohibited from discussing budget figures with anyone outside the finance section. Any violation of these guidelines will be treated as a serious offense and will lead to immediate termination of employment. Operators who follow these guidelines perfectly will receive a special recognition from the finance secretary. These guidelines are part of the government's commitment to financial transparency and accountability.

documents.title: Training Program for New Computer Operators
documents.text: The National Computer Training Center has announced a comprehensive training program for all newly appointed computer operators in government service. The training program will last for fifteen working days and will be conducted at the training center in Dhaka. Accommodation and food will be provided by the government for outstation participants. The training program covers the following topics. The first topic is touch typing technique including correct finger placement on the home row and proper posture. The second topic is speed building exercises designed to help participants reach the required thirty five words per minute. The third topic is accuracy improvement strategies including error detection and correction methods. The fourth topic is the standard format for typing official letters, memos, and circulars. The fifth topic is the use of shortcut keys to increase productivity. The sixth topic is file management and maintenance of the digital register. The seventh topic is data entry techniques for numerical and mixed data. The eighth topic is basic computer maintenance and troubleshooting. The ninth topic is the code of conduct for government typists. The tenth topic is handling urgent and emergency typing tasks. At the end of the training program, participants must pass a final examination consisting of a five minute typing test and a short written test. Those who fail the final examination will have to repeat the training program. Successful participants will receive a training completion certificate which will be placed in their personal file.

documents.title: Notification on Public Service Delivery
documents.text: The Cabinet Division has issued a notification emphasizing the role of computer operators in delivering efficient public services to the citizens of Bangladesh. Every day, thousands of citizens visit government offices to obtain various certificates, licenses, and approvals. The quality of service they receive depends significantly on the speed and accuracy of the computer operators who type their documents. A slow or error prone operator can cause long waiting times and unnecessary frustration for citizens. Therefore, every computer operator must treat each citizen with respect and professionalism. When a citizen submits an application, the operator must type the relevant document without unnecessary delay. If the operator is unsure about any detail, they must politely ask the citizen for clarification rather than guessing. After typing the document, the operator must read it aloud to the citizen to confirm that all information is correct. If the citizen identifies an error, the operator must correct it immediately without argument. The notification also states that any operator who receives three or more formal complaints from citizens in a single month will be required to attend a customer service training program. Operators who receive appreciation letters from citizens will have those letters placed in their annual confidential report. The government is committed to providing fast, accurate, and respectful service to every citizen, and computer operators are essential to achieving this goal.

documents.title: Instructions for Computer Maintenance
documents.text: The Information Technology Division has issued detailed instructions for computer operators regarding the basic maintenance of their office computers. Proper maintenance of the computer and keyboard is essential for consistent typing performance. Every operator must follow these instructions at the beginning and end of each working day. First, before turning on the computer, inspect the keyboard for any dust, food particles, or liquid spills. If the keyboard is dirty, gently clean it with a soft dry cloth. Never pour water or cleaning liquid directly onto the keyboard. Second, check that all cables are securely connected to the computer and the power outlet. Third, after turning on the computer, check that the keyboard is responding properly by typing a few test sentences. Fourth, during the day, avoid eating or drinking near the keyboard to prevent spills and crumbs. Fifth, at the end of the day, close all open documents and properly shut down the computer using the operating system shutdown command. Never turn off the computer by directly pressing the power button. Sixth, cover the keyboard with a clean cloth to protect it from dust overnight. If any key stops working or feels stuck, the operator must immediately report the issue to the IT section. Do not attempt to remove or repair any key without authorization. Regular maintenance of the computer and keyboard will extend their life and ensure smooth typing performance for all operators in the section.

documents.title: Circular on Prevention of Typing Errors
documents.text: The Ministry of Public Administration has issued a circular on the prevention of typing errors in official correspondence. Typing errors in government documents not only cause confusion but also damage the reputation of the office. The circular introduces a three step verification system to minimize errors. In the first step, the computer operator who types the document must read it carefully from beginning to end before printing. In the second step, a senior operator or section officer must read the printed document and mark any remaining errors with a red pen. In the third step, the original operator must correct all marked errors and print a fresh copy. The circular also lists the most common types of typing errors observed in government offices. These include missing punctuation marks, incorrect capitalization, extra spaces between words, spelling mistakes in commonly used words, and typographical errors in numerical data. To help operators avoid these errors, the ministry has prepared a list of one hundred commonly misspelled words which will be distributed to every section. Operators are encouraged to practice typing these words until they can type them correctly without thinking. The circular also states that every section must maintain an error log where all typing errors are recorded along with the name of the operator responsible. Sections that achieve a zero error rate for three consecutive months will receive a certificate of excellence from the ministry. This circular is part of the government's ongoing effort to improve the quality of official communication.

documents.title: Final Preparation Tips for Typing Examination
documents.text: The Bangladesh Public Service Commission has published a set of final preparation tips for all candidates who will appear in the upcoming typing examination for computer operator positions. These tips are based on the observations of previous examination panels and are intended to help candidates perform at their best on the day of the test. Tip number one is to practice daily on a standard desktop keyboard rather than a laptop keyboard because the examination center will use desktop computers. Tip number two is to focus on accuracy during the first three minutes of the test before trying to increase speed. Tip number three is to keep your eyes on the source text on the screen rather than looking down at your fingers. Tip number four is to maintain a steady breathing rhythm to keep your hands relaxed and prevent cramping. Tip number five is that if you make a mistake, correct it with a single backspace and continue without panicking. Tip number six is to arrive at the examination center at least thirty minutes early to avoid any last minute stress. Tip number seven is to get a good night's sleep before the examination day because a tired mind makes more errors. Tip number eight is to eat a light meal before the test because a heavy meal can make you feel sleepy. Tip number nine is to bring your original ID card and printed admit card. Tip number ten is to stay calm and confident because nervousness is the biggest enemy of accurate typing. The commission wishes all candidates the very best of luck for their examination.
